record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the referenced RESULTS.md, notebook, scripts, and result files were not provided as readable contents.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports ablation results using the difference-in-means refusal direction, including an every-layer test on Qwen and single-layer tests across Gemma models. The method is close to the original, but the Gemma tests use a different intervention scope and the README is not a complete study text.
record.gate_note: Rows record README-reported outcomes only. The README describes how the direction is extracted and lists files and scripts, but those descriptions are not additional experimental results. The cited multi-direction findings and the suggested need for multi-direction interventions are not results of this repository.
record.test_reason: The study re-applies difference-in-means extraction and projection-out ablation to Qwen 2.5 and Gemma 2/3/4 and reports refusal-removal outcomes. Qwen uses every-layer ablation, close to the original. The Gemma matrix uses single-layer hooks, a narrower intervention than V1 describes. Only the README was readable.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say the ablation works cleanly on Qwen 2.5 1.5B (every-layer) and on Gemma 3 with a single hook in a subset of cells. Single-layer ablation largely fails on Gemma 2 and Gemma 4. They attribute Gemma 3's outlier sensitivity to inflated post-norm gains. They state the direction is not a noise artifact, given the random-vector control. They suggest, without testing, that Gemma 2/4 need multi-direction (cone) interventions or higher-magnitude protocols.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-harmless mean activations and projection-out ablation, but extracts the direction from last-token residual activations. The README reports every-layer ablation for Qwen and single-layer matrix tests for Gemma, not a uniform intervention at every layer and position. Repository README describes this as a cross-family replication study; underlying files and results were not read.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports a strong model-family difference and varied outcomes across cells in the Gemma 3 and Gemma 2 5×3 block-by-direction matrices.

fits_no_version.finding: Gemma 3 post-attention and post-feedforward RMSNorm mean |gain| is 5–30× larger than in Gemma 2 or Qwen. The authors propose this explains Gemma 3's sensitivity to single-layer ablation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architectural normalization gains modulate how strongly a single-layer refusal-direction ablation propagates to behaviour.

record.problems: The repository contents beyond the README and file list were not available in the supplied text. The Qwen result is reported on a 12-prompt set but gives a 10/10 outcome denominator; the README does not explain the discrepancy. Gemma results are summarized as aggregate cell counts without individual cell outcomes, baselines, or uncertainty estimates. No general-capability evaluation is reported in the README.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the experimental results summarized in the README. The listed RMSNorm measurements and mechanistic explanation are not findings on refusal behavior named by the claim versions; detailed results are in the unavailable RESULTS.md and result files.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts: an amplification script and alpha scan exist, but the README reports no results. Any general-capability evaluation beyond a coherence heuristic. Every-layer ablation results on Gemma 2 and Gemma 4.
Multi-direction or cone ablation is proposed as future work only; the authors' suggestion that Gemma 2/4 need it is untested.

missing.what: Every-layer ablation on Gemma 3 appears to yield degenerate rather than coherent output: the queued alpha<1 test aims to 'recover coherent jailbreak instead of degenerate output'. This bears on V1's claim that other abilities are kept. The exact numbers are not in the README.
missing.locator: README, Status & next directions item 2; RESULTS.md (not read)

missing.what: Qwen 0.5B and 3B results: ASR-vs-depth layer sweeps and an amplification alpha scan are listed as result files but not summarized in the README.

record.verdict_notes: I relabelled r4 from challenges to limits_scope: V1 describes every-layer ablation, and the Gemma 4 test was single-layer only. This is not an original source. The evidence is README-only; RESULTS.md, which records many retractions, was unavailable, so the headline numbers may not reflect final findings.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports removal/ablation results, but no result for adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests. It does not establish that general abilities are largely intact; the Qwen result reports coherent versus degenerate outputs, not a general-capability evaluation. The README describes the Gemma tests as single-layer, not the full every-layer-and-position intervention.
No reported weight edit or released-model abliteration result.
No reported test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
Multi-direction interventions are listed as future work; the README does not report testing affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
The README reports extracting directions separately for model checkpoints. It does not test whether one direction transfers across models, languages, or base-to-instruct variants.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing.
